claims.text: A transaction script is one method that runs a whole business operation step by step (typically check input, load or build data, change, save, report; a step may be skipped), over data that holds no rules of its own.
The pattern name comes from the book Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture, where 'transaction' means a business operation, not a database transaction.
claims.source_hint: Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture, Transaction Script (bare reference; no source in versions.yaml)

claims.text: At stage-1 CancelOrderAsync finds the order (repository.FindAsync, KeyNotFoundException if missing), sets order.Status = "cancelled", calls SaveChangesAsync, then notifier.Send; it never reads the current status first.

At stage-1 PlaceOrderAsync throws ArgumentException for an empty item list, builds an Order with an object initializer (CustomerId, PlacedAt, Status = "new", Items), calls AddAsync, SaveChangesAsync, then notifier.Send.
At stage-1 Order has a public getter and setter for every property and no methods, so a rule about which status may follow which has no place in Order; in this design it is written in the script.

No code in stage-1 OrderService opens a database transaction (no BeginTransaction, the call that opens one in code); FindAsync's query and the final save each go to the database on their own, so no single transaction covers the whole method.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: OrderService.cs, EfOrderRepository.cs; EF Core docs: Transactions, default transaction behavior

claims.text: The stage-1 comment on CancelOrderAsync says an order already shipped still gets cancelled and DonHang.Tests covers new but not shipped.
A transaction script is easy to follow while an operation has few rules; when several scripts change the same data, each needs its own copy of the checks and nothing forces a new script to add them.
A transaction script is a simple design that works well while operations share few rules; when data has no rules, a script is often clearer than spreading a few lines across classes.

At stage-1, git grep -n "Status" -- "DonHang.Domain/*.cs" prints three lines: Entities.cs:30 (declaration with public setter), OrderService.cs:16 (Status = "new") and OrderService.cs:34 (order.Status = "cancelled").

claims.text: The orders table allows status values new, paid, shipped and cancelled; shipping is not implemented at stage-1 (no ShipOrderAsync).
